name: R2-10 DEV-only predictor selection rule (frozen before any DEV result exists)
eval_influence: FORBIDDEN -- no EVAL result may influence family/config selection; mirrors R2-09B/R2-09A b_selected_rule.eval_hindsight_diagnostic_only discipline.
pool: families.causal_runtime_candidates from predictor_space.json only (global_frequency, last_observation, and -- once implemented in the DEV tournament phase -- recency_window, markov_transition, decayed_transition, recency_frequency_transition_blend). shuffled_null is never in the pool.

aggregation.primary_selection_statistic: mean future_requested_expert_recall_at_k over the primary horizon h=1, equal weight per DEV instance (macro by instance, NOT token-weighted and NOT layer-weighted), matching the equal-per-instance weighting style already frozen for R2-09A's B_selected rule.
aggregation.formula: Score(family, config) = mean over the 8 DEV cells of [ mean over all (t, l, h=1) targets in that cell of recall_at_k(t,l) ]
aggregation.weights: equal weight per DEV instance (8 cells); within a cell, equal weight per (t,l) target (token/layer weighted equally within-instance, never instance-count-of-targets-weighted across instances) -- this prevents a longer trace (e.g. 511 vs 381 decode steps) from dominating the cross-instance average.
aggregation.secondary_horizons_reporting: h=4 and h=16 are reported descriptively per family/config using the same aggregation, but are NEVER used in the primary selection statistic (matches predictor_space.json / prediction_contract.json horizon primacy of h=1).

tie_breaking: 3. lexical config_id ascending (deterministic fallback, same convention as R2-09A's B_selected tie-break)
freeze_requirement: This selection rule is frozen in this Phase-0 contract BEFORE any DEV result exists for recency_window, markov_transition, decayed_transition, or the blend (only global_frequency/last_observation have been exercised at all in Phase 0, and only for contract/leakage/determinism testing on a synthetic trace, never for a selection decision).
